bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the Rucio WebUI rule-approval flow: an authenticated low-privilege user can submit attacker-controlled HTML/JavaScript in POST /proxy/rules/ as the rule comment. The backend persists that value in the rule's comments field and list_rules returns it. approve_rules.js copied the entire server object into a DataTables data source and declared the comments property as a display column without a text renderer or output encoding, so DataTables inserted the stored value as HTML when an administrator reviewed waiting-approval rules. Script then executes in the WebUI origin, with the victim's session/API-token authority. The advisory also identifies a rule-detail viewing trigger; the directly demonstrated root sink in history is the unescaped approval-table comments column.
flaw_origin: Commit 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f created lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js and, in one atomic feature commit, introduced the vulnerable chain: list_rules server data is pushed unchanged into filtered_data, passed to DataTable, and the raw {'data': 'comments'} property is displayed. The immediate parent already accepted and persisted rule comments through the REST/API/core path, but had no approve_rules.js sink, so this is the smallest first-writer rather than a later move, refactor, release commit, or squash.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f` shows author and committer Thomas Beermann <thomas.beermann@cern.ch>, the subject '[RUCIO-1723] page to show rules in approval state', and only a Gerrit Change-Id trailer. It contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: In the validated clone, `git show db48889e085355dbc31657a4719cc49f813c64b7:lib/rucio/web/rest/rule.py` at POST lines 160-240 shows pre-BIC request parsing of params['comment'] and forwarding it to add_replication_rule; `git grep -n comment db48889e085355dbc31657a4719cc49f813c64b7 -- lib/rucio/api/rule.py lib/rucio/core/rule.py` shows the API/core persistence path and Rule.comments storage. `git log --all -S"{'data': 'comments'" -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js` returns only 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f as the first addition. `git log -L '/get_rules = function/',+70:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003^` independently traces the unchanged filtered_data/DataTable/comments chain back to that file-creation commit; blame of lines 45-110 agrees. `git cat-file -p 010746bc16b72313d1e779fa9a15996c44b40a9f` gives parent db48889e085355dbc31657a4719cc49f813c64b7 and the marker evidence above. Direct parent verification with `git cat-file -e db48889e085355dbc31657a4719cc49f813c64b7:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js` fails because the file does not exist, while the BIC creates the 306-line file. `git grep -n "{'data': 'comments'" 1.3.0.post1 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js` finds the sink; the same file is absent at 1.2.5.post4. On the default branch, `git show b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/approve_rules.js` is the direct GHSA-rwj9-7j48-9f7q fix: its parent has raw {'data': 'comments'} and the fix replaces pass-through rows with an explicit object whose comments value is encoded via $('<div>').text(value.comments).html(). Release-line equivalents are a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003 (35.x), abf5e978ee3910590a23c6705e6a0105c0b847c7 (38.x), and 80b91dd0c6737b2ab9aed039470e8e81028def41 (39.x). `git grep` finds the raw comments column in 35.8.2 (eaebc315c5a4a6721c6744a27a07ad22a9586ff0), 38.5.3 (4fd064e67f4979bf83222a5ad95eb12054e63b59), and 39.3.0 (994beeb0dcad09b75bbb486cf9c58a7d469562e5), but the encoded comments assignment in first-patched 35.8.3 (ba9203702629af7bb1f95d5cf9ba8fcf1f943105), 38.5.4 (c851ad216e0e0e3d50405eab3331dfe21c96ddd3), and 39.3.1 (ba2a7e66b1e3c73b5cf9e0000e6621e8dc45bfe7), matching the advisory's three version ranges.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by the browser sink, not by the longstanding ability to store a rule comment: before the BIC, the source and persistence path existed but no approval-page JavaScript consumed comments as DataTables HTML. The BIC creates that complete unsafe renderer; -S, -L, blame, and direct-parent object checks converge on it, and later edits only preserve or modify surrounding behavior. The default-branch security commit directly encodes comments before DataTables rendering, with equivalent coordinated backports establishing every advertised patch boundary. Because the BIC is a normal 2015 human-authored Gerrit commit with no explicit AI attribution or bot identity, BIC-only attribution requires NOT_AI; AI status of the 2026 fix is irrelevant.
